subject: Re: convergence failure of otherwise good model

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: convergence failure of otherwise good model
parts:
Hi Eric,

Can you send me the project file (do File | Export Project... and save=20
as a zip file) and I'll take a look at it -- I don't understand why it's=20
not converging. Perhaps setting bounds on the parameters will help.

Cheers,

- len

Eric D. Stolen wrote:
> > I have a question about how to proceed with an analysis in which there =
is=20
> > a convergence failure for a model that otherwise looks like the best mo=
del=20
> > for the detection function. This is an analysis of an aerial survey of=
=20
> > bottlenose dolphins in a shallow lagoon system in Florida. Following d=
ata=20
> > screening, I decided on analysis of ungrouped data with data truncated =
at=20
> > 273 m (9.3% observations, original data range 0-736 m). I tried six=20
> > models for the detection function (Half-normal Key with both cosine and=
=20
> > hermite polynomial, Uniform key with both simple polynomial and cosine,=
=20
> > and hazard-rate key with both simple polynomial and cosine). The Unifo=
rm=20
> > key with simple polynomial series expansion and 1 adjustment terms had =
the=20
> > lowest AIC. The next best model was Uniform, cosine (AIC=3D3.64), then=
Half-
> > normal cosine (AIC=3D6.49). However, the Uniform/simple model with 1=20
> > adjustment term failed to converge, but was still selected as the best=20
> > model. =20
> >=20
> > Looking at the iteration history for this model, I see that by the seve=
nth=20
> > iteration, the likelihood stays very close to -1250 and the estimate of=
A
> > (1) stays very close to -1.07. I tried setting the starting value near=
=20
> > where the convergence left off, but after many attempts, I was not able=
to=20
> > get it to converge. =20
> >=20
> > I next tried fitting the same models to the data grouped into six=20
> > intervals. Again, the Uniform, simple polynomial (with 1 adjustment ter=
m)=20
> > was the best model, and this time the model converged. However, the=20
> > detection function was slightly different between the two analyses: {f(=
0)
> > ungrouped =3D 0.00569 vs. f(0)grouped =3D 0.00533; A(1)ungrouped =3D -1=
.074 vs. A
> > (1)grouped =3D -0.938}. The precision for the grouped data was lower=20
> > (CVungrouped =3D 10.0%, CVgrouped =3D 10.5%), and the density estimates=
were=20
> > slightly different (ungrouped =3D 0.0050194, grouped =3D 0.0046979). =20
> >=20
> > This analysis is of one geographic strata within a larger analysis=20
> > comprised of four geographic strata. I have decided on using separate=
=20
> > detection function models between geographic strata, based on compariso=
n=20
> > of the AIC of pooled verses separate data. I=92d like to use the ungro=
uped=20
> > data in this geographic strata, to be consistent with how the other=20
> > geographic starta are being treated. Although the is a moderate amount=
of=20
> > heaping in the data (due to use of an inclinometer to measure angles fr=
om=20
> > the survey aircraft which were later converted into perpendicular=20
> > distances), the analyses of ungrouped data have performed very well for=
=20
> > the other three geographic strata.
> >=20
> > To refocus on my questions, I=92m wondering if I can I trusted the para=
meter=20
> > estimates of the model that failed to converge, or should I use the=20
> > grouped data analysis? Or is there another way to proceed?
> >=20
